items.readable_text:
Content:
Given a sphere with radius [MATH: r= 3\:\textrm{cm},] how do we calculate its volume?

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f54b4469f4f650b1fdc27e6a06f7f02f]

Content:
In general, we can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

Content:
[MATH: V= \dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3,]

Content:
where [MATH: r] is the radius of the sphere.

Content:
Substituting [MATH: r=3\:\textrm{cm}] into the formula, we obtain

Content:
[MATH: V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi \cdot (3)^3
=36 \pi \:\textrm{cm}^3.]

Content:
We often express the volume of a sphere as a multiple of [MATH: \pi.] However, we can also use a calculator to get a numerical approximation. In this case, we get

Content:
[MATH: V \approx 113.10 \:\textrm{cm}^3]

Content:
rounded to two decimal places.

sections.normalized_html:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula [MATH: V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3 ,] where [MATH: r] is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting [MATH: V=36\pi\:\textrm{in}^3] into the formula, we get [MATH: V|= (4)/(3)πr^{3}; 36π|= (4)/(3)πr^{3}; 36π ⋅ (3)/(4π)|= r^{3}; r^{3}|= 27.]

Therefore, [MATH: r = \sqrt[3]{27} = 3\:\textrm{in}.]
